'''Dietrich Braess''' (born 16 June 1938) is a German mathematician. He is known for [[Braess's paradox]], which deals with [[Traffic congestion|traffic]] [[List of types of equilibrium|equilibrium]].<ref>{{cite web|author=Dietrich Braess |url=http://homepage.ruhr-uni-bochum.de/dietrich.braess/#paradox |title=D. Braess |publisher=Homepage.ruhr-uni-bochum.de |date= |accessdate=2013-03-04}}</ref> Braess's focus has centered on numerical treatment of elliptical [[Differential equation|differential equations]] and nonlinear approximation theories.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://homepage.ruhr-uni-bochum.de/Dietrich.Braess/#eng|title=D. Braess|last=Braess|first=Dietrich|website=homepage.ruhr-uni-bochum.de|access-date=2018-10-19}}</ref>
